reasoning: The test image shows a banana leaf with classic marginal yellowing: a wide yellow band at the leaf edge with brown necrotic tissue at the outermost margin and a wave-like irregular boundary progressing into the green interior. This marginal yellowing pattern — starting at leaf edges and progressing inward — is characteristic of Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt), which disrupts vascular transport causing peripheral leaf yellowing and necrosis. The pattern does not match scattered/oval spots (Cordana Leaf Spot, Anthracnose) or vein-streak patterns (Sigatoka), nor fruit-specific (Cigar End Rot) or systemic stunting (Bunchy Top) diseases.
